sangeeta: FYI I noticed a small-batch p95 microstutter in prod after merging PR #3124 (fused softmax/scale). Noticed on streaming chat with batch=1, seq=1024. Can folks help triage? :mag:

I need: a) quick microbench across implementations (flash vs paged vs fused) for batch 1/2/4, seq 256/512/1024, b) nvprof/nsight traces for the fused softmax path for batch=1, c) any config flags we can toggle to avoid the blip (if kernel startup is the culprit).

Example bench command I ran locally (please run on rgx pools if possible):
```
./ci/bench.py --model=llama-70b --impl=flash,paged,fused --seq=1024,512,256 --batch=1,2,4 --warmup=30 --iters=120 --streaming
```

Please paste results in this thread. Thanks!

---

todd: tagging infra/bench: I'll run a sweep on rgx-pool-4 and rgx-pool-6, schedule now. Can you paste the exact PR hash for #3124 and which image rolled to prod? Also, add `--collect-trace=nvtx` to capture NVTX ranges.

sangeeta: PR is https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/3124 diff 7f3a9c. Prod image is build-20260315-rc3.

jamal: I can run quick microbench on rgx-pool-4 now. Running the exact command with --impl=flash,paged,fused and will post p50/p95. Will also try with `--prefetch-kv=on` and `--pad-to=64`.

deploy-bot: canary: build-20260315-rc3 rolled to staging (rgx-pool-4) at 2026-03-15T14:12:03Z :rocket:

jamal: quick numbers (rgx-pool-4, single run, warmup 30 iters):
- flash (batch=1, seq=1024): p50=48ms p95=110ms
- paged (batch=1, seq=1024): p50=46ms p95=112ms
- fused (batch=1, seq=1024): p50=55ms p95=255ms <-- big tail

Observed that fused increases p95 hugely for batch=1. For batch=4 differences are small. Looks like kernel launch/serialization on fused path when sequence large and batch small. :confused:

sangeeta: thanks jamal. That matches prod symptoms. Todd/everyone: can you capture `nvprof --profile-child-processes` or nsight for fused-case batch=1 and attach timeline? We need to know if it's kernel enqueue latency or something inside kernel (softmax reduction stalls).

evelyn: some quick thoughts: 1) check kv-cache memory alignment & padding (we've seen unaligned loads cause extra memcpy), 2) fused path changed softmax -> exp+sum reduction ordering, might be triggering a different shared-memory pattern for long seq. Try `--kv-align=64` and `--reduce-chunk=32` toggles. Also consider a quick fallback: skip fused-softmax for batch==1 & seq>512 until we pinpoint (cheap guard).

andre: I sketched a tiny patch to fall back to flash when (batch_size == 1 && seq_len > 512) and avoid launching fused kernel. It's safe perf-wise for now and bounded. I'll open a draft PR and tag it `hotfix/microstutter`.

andre: patch gist snippet:```cpp
if (batch == 1 && seq > 512 && impl == Impl::Fused) {
  impl = Impl::Flash; // fallback to pre-optimized flash attention
}
```

todd: running nsight capture now on rgx-pool-6 fused batch=1 seq=1024, will upload timeline. Adding CUPTI latency counters and kernel launch timestamps. ETA ~40m.

jamal: added a small experiment: enabling `--pad-to=64` reduced fused p95 from 255ms -> 130ms, p50 ~52ms. So padding helps but doesn't fully eliminate tail. Suspect reduction warp divergence when tensor shapes not multiple of warp size.

sangeeta: good find. If padding has that big effect we could add automatic pad-to-64 for fused kernels as a temporary mitigation. But want to understand cost (extra memory + fill overhead). Jamal, please run memory delta check for pad-on vs pad-off.

jamal: will run memory/throughput delta. Preliminary: extra ~3% VRAM at seq=1024, batch=1. Throughput unchanged for batch>1.

evelyn: another angle: check launcher threads and CUDA stream synchronization around the fused kernel; we had a scheduler change that serializes some enqueue operations for fused kernels because of semaphore handling. If the semaphore path executes on the host then batch=1 sequences might block. I'll grep for recent semaphore changes in scheduler.

andre: opened draft PR https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/3187 that implements the batch==1 fallback + auto pad-to-64 toggle behind feature flag `runtime.fused_autopad=true`. Marking as WIP.

sangeeta: thanks Andre. Can we also add a tiny canary job in CI that runs fused path for batch=1/seq=1024 and fails if p95 > 200ms? Might prevent future regressions.

todd: agree. I'll add a bench smoke in circleci `eng-runtime-smoke` pipeline: run fused batch=1 seq=1024 on a cheap instance; threshold p95<=200ms. Will submit a patch after I have nsight traces.

jamal: uploaded nvprof timeline and a short flamechart to the gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/abc123 (contains nvprof csv + screenshot). The timeline shows a ~120ms gap between kernel enqueue and kernel execution for the fused case, and then a heavy kernel runtime ~100ms. Looks like both enqueue delay + long kernel contribute.

sangeeta: perfect. This gives two levers: avoid enqueue penalty (scheduler fix) and reduce kernel runtime (autopad / kernel micro-optim). For now let's: 1) merge Andre's hotfix behind flag to quickly reduce customer impact, 2) todd adds CI smoke, 3) evelyn + eng-runtime to investigate scheduler semaphore path and fused kernel inner reduce.

todd: logged ticket RT-4872 for scheduler investigation and assigned to evelyn. I'll also create CI job PR.

evelyn: ack RT-4872, will look at semaphore enqueue path and post findings here. If I find simple fix I'll bench before prod roll.

sangeeta: awesome. Thanks all. Please paste any follow-ups/traces here. If someone has capacity to prod-canary the hotfix flag in staging tonight that would be great. :thumbsup:

jamal: I can flip the feature flag in staging after Andre's PR is ready.

andre: will mark PR as ready for review in ~30m.
